main_issue: Whether and when Agent D can cook strong-smelling salted fish in the shared flat, and what arrangement limits the smell's impact on the others.

A-B.evidence: Turn 2 B agrees with A's ban request; later B says the time doesn't matter (13) and accepts a heads-up arrangement (21) instead of a ban. A and B never address each other after turn 2.

A-C.evidence: Turn 3 C backs A's complaint; later C accepts weekend cooking with advance notice (25, 29), which fits A's accepted once-a-week weekend plan (16). They never address each other directly.

A-D.evidence: D opposes a ban (4) and asks to discuss timing (8); A agrees (9). D offers a check-in (10) and weekend once a week (15), and A accepts: 'That works for me' (16).

B-C.evidence: Both complain about smell (2, 3), say time doesn't help (13, 14), object to the weekend plan (17, 18), and each accept a notice-based accommodation (21, 25).

B-D.evidence: B objects (17), then offers 'If you just tell me before you start, I can close my door' (21); D replies 'Okay, I can let you know' (22) and later confirms the plan (26).

C-D.evidence: C says laundry will still get the smell (18); D asks C directly (22); C proposes avoiding laundry on the cooking day if told (25); D 'Okay, that works' (26); C 'works for me' (29).
